## Overview

This document quantifies spatial uncertainty in the ATE by simulating predicted mortality counts from two fitted spaMM models (`fitmort_child_gen_krig` and `fitmort_child_gen_krig_int`) and computing the posterior probability that the treatment effect is beneficial at each grid location.

The workflow:

1. Construct a prediction dataset covering all grid locations × both treatment arms.
2. Simulate `nsim_input` draws from each model's predictive distribution using `type = "predVar"`, which incorporates both fixed-effect (linear predictor) uncertainty and Poisson dispersion.
3. For each simulation and grid point, compute the simulated ATE (`pred_Treatment - pred_Control`).
4. Estimate the posterior probability of a beneficial ATE as the proportion of simulations where this difference is negative (lower mortality under treatment).

```{r load data, warning=F, message=F}

source(here::here("analysis", "0-config.R"))

re_simulate <- FALSE # Set TRUE to re-run simulations (slow: ~13 min per model)

b_boxgrid <- readRDS(here("data", "boxgrid.rds"))

# Load the two models used for posterior simulation:
# gen_krig: generalized kriging without treatment×location interaction
# gen_krig_int: generalized kriging with treatment×lat and treatment×lon interactions
fitmort_child_gen_krig_int <- readRDS(here("data", "fitmort_child_gen_krig_int.rds"))
fitmort_child_gen_krig <- readRDS(here("data", "fitmort_child_gen_krig.rds"))
```

---

## Simulate predictive responses

Prediction data (`newdat`) is constructed by crossing both treatment arm labels with all grid locations. Each row represents a hypothetical observation at a grid centroid under one treatment arm. `pt_year_1to59 = 1000` is the standard offset used throughout this analysis (predictions are on the per-1,000-person-years scale). `site_code` is not included because neither model contains a `site_code` random effect.

Simulations use `type = "predVar"` with `variances = list(linPred = TRUE, disp = TRUE)` to sample from the full predictive distribution: uncertainty in the linear predictor (spatial random effect + fixed effects) plus Poisson count dispersion. The number of simulations is controlled by `nsim_input` (set in `0-config.R`).

Simulations took 789.3 sec (13.2 min) for the generalized kriging model without interaction and 765.641 sec (12.8 min) for the model with interaction.

```{r simulate responses}

# Cross-join grid locations with both treatment arms to get one row per location × arm
newdat <- cross_join(
  tibble(isTreated_child = c("Treatment", "Control")),
  b_boxgrid
) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1],
         lat = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2],
         pt_year_1to59 = 1000,   # offset: predictions on per-1000-person-years scale
         isTreated_child = factor(isTreated_child)) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()

# Simulate from predictive distribution including both linear predictor
# uncertainty (linPred=TRUE) and Poisson count dispersion (disp=TRUE)

if(re_simulate){

  tic("simulations")
  simulated_responses_gen_krig <- simulate(fitmort_child_gen_krig,
                                      type = "predVar",
                                      variances=list(linPred=TRUE,disp=TRUE),
                                      nsim = nsim_input,
                                      newdata = newdat,
                                      seed = 12345
  )
  toc()

  saveRDS(simulated_responses_gen_krig, here("data", "simulated_responses_gen_krig.rds"))

  tic("simulations: interaction")
  simulated_responses_gen_krig_int <- simulate(fitmort_child_gen_krig_int,
                                      type = "predVar",
                                      variances=list(linPred=TRUE,disp=TRUE),
                                      nsim = nsim_input,
                                      newdata = newdat,
                                      seed = 12345
  )
  toc()

  saveRDS(simulated_responses_gen_krig_int, here("data", "simulated_responses_gen_krig_int.rds"))

} else {
  simulated_responses_gen_krig <- readRDS(here("data", "simulated_responses_gen_krig.rds"))
  simulated_responses_gen_krig_int <- readRDS(here("data", "simulated_responses_gen_krig_int.rds"))
}

```

---

## Post-process simulations

`sim2tib()` converts the raw simulation matrix (rows = grid locations × arms, columns = simulations) into a long-format tibble with one row per location × arm × simulation, then pivots to wide form so Treatment and Control predictions are in separate columns for each simulation draw.

`ate_resp = pred_Treatment - pred_Control` is the simulated ATE at each location and simulation. For a mortality outcome, **negative values indicate a beneficial treatment effect** (fewer deaths under treatment).

```{r post process simulations}

# sim2tib: converts a spaMM simulation matrix to a tidy long-format tibble
# sim_responses : matrix output of spaMM::simulate() — rows = newdat rows, cols = simulations
# newdat        : the prediction dataset used in simulate() (must be same row order)
# modelname     : character label added to the output for faceting/grouping
sim2tib <- function(sim_responses, newdat, modelname = NA_character_){
  # convert matrix to tibble and name sim columns
  sim_tibs <- as_tibble(
    sim_responses,
    .name_repair = ~ paste0("sim_", seq_along(.))
  )

  # bind the coordinates / covariates (keep ordering)
  combined <- bind_cols(
    newdat %>% dplyr::select(lon, lat, isTreated_child),
    sim_tibs
  )

  # pivot to long form
  long_preds <- combined %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("sim_"),
      names_to = "sim",
      values_to = "pred"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      sim_n = as.integer(sub("^sim_", "", sim))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(lon, lat, isTreated_child, sim_n, pred) %>%
    mutate(model = modelname)

}

full_pred_long <- rbind(
  sim2tib(simulated_responses_gen_krig, newdat, "gen_krig"),
  sim2tib(simulated_responses_gen_krig_int, newdat, "gen_krig_int")
)

# Pivot wide: one row per location × simulation, Treatment and Control as separate columns
full_pred <- full_pred_long %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(lon, lat, sim_n, model),
  names_from = isTreated_child, names_prefix = "pred_",
  values_from = pred)

# Simulated ATE: negative = beneficial (lower mortality under treatment)
full_pred <- full_pred %>%
  mutate(ate_resp = pred_Treatment - pred_Control)

saveRDS(full_pred, here("data", "full_pred_sim.rds"))
```

---

## Posterior probability of beneficial ATE

For each grid location, the posterior probability of a beneficial treatment effect is the proportion of simulations where `ate_resp < 0` (treatment arm has lower predicted mortality than control). Values near 1 indicate strong evidence of benefit; values near 0.5 indicate uncertainty; values near 0 suggest potential harm.

```{r posterior probability}

post_prob <- full_pred %>%
  group_by(lon, lat, model) %>%
  summarise(neg_ate = sum(ifelse(ate_resp < 0, 1, 0)),  # count of simulations with beneficial ATE
  total_ate = n(),
  prob = neg_ate/total_ate,  # posterior probability of beneficial ATE
  .groups = "drop")

post_prob_map <- post_prob %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = proj_crs)

saveRDS(post_prob_map, here("data", "post_prob_dat.rds"))

```

---

## Simulation diagnostics

### Distribution of simulated ATE

Summary statistics and boxplots of `ate_resp` across all grid points and simulations, and the distribution of posterior probabilities across grid locations. The median `prob` near 0.5 would indicate overall uncertainty; systematic shift toward 1 would indicate consistent spatial evidence of benefit.

```{r calculate sim summ metrics}

summary(full_pred$ate_resp)

summary(post_prob$prob)

ggplot(data = post_prob, aes(color = model, group = model)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = prob, y = model))

```

### Simulated ATE distribution by model

Full distribution of simulated ATEs across all grid locations, comparing models with and without the treatment × location interaction. The panel without outliers shows the bulk of the distribution more clearly.

```{r plot sim dist}
sim_box <- ggplot(data = full_pred, aes(group = model, color = model, y = model)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = ate_resp)) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())

sim_box_no_ol <- ggplot(data = full_pred, aes(group = model, color = model, y = model)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = ate_resp), outliers = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed") +
  guides(color = "none") +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(),
  axis.text.y = element_blank())

sim_box | sim_box_no_ol +
  plot_annotation(title = "Summary across all simulations, all grid points")
```

### Sample of individual simulation draws

Ten randomly selected simulation draws, faceted by model. Each boxplot shows the distribution of simulated ATEs across grid locations for a single draw — this illustrates within-simulation spatial variation in the ATE.

```{r plot sample sim}
sim_sub_idx <- sample(1:nsim_input, size = 10, replace = FALSE)
sim_sub <- full_pred %>%
  dplyr::filter(sim_n %in% sim_sub_idx)

ggplot(data = sim_sub, aes(group = sim_n, color = model, y = factor(sim_n))) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = ate_resp), outliers = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 2) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  ggtitle("10 random simulations")

```
